To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

patients with CLBP treated by instrumented spinal fusion had a similar outcome at 9-year follow-up as patients treated with cognitive intervention and exercises, although more operated patients used medication and were out-of-work.

there was no difference between the two treatments in the intention-to-treat analyses and that the patients allocated to cognitive intervention and exercise used less pain medication and were more often at work than the patients allocated to fusion, if we look only at patients that received the treatment they were randomized to.
the outcome at 9 years was not different between patients treated with instrumented lumbar surgery and patients treated with cognitive intervention and exercises.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of high performance materials for the treatment of chronic low back pain.
the question of whether lumbar fusion is superior to non-surgical treatment for low back pain.
the development of a method of analysis of the effects of treatment of low back pain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results at 9-year follow-up are not different between lumbar fusion and a non-surgical treatment approach in patients with chronic LBP.
there is no difference in outcome between instrumented lumback fusion and cognitive intervention with exercises in chronic low back pain patients.
the two treatments are equally ineffective in the long term.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the patients who crossed over from the cognitive intervention and exercises group had better outcomes at 1 and 9 years than the patients in the fusion group.
the patients randomized to fusion did not have better outcome than the patients randomized to exercises and cognitive intervention.

lumbar fusion is not superior to cognitive intervention and exercise for patients with chronic low-back pain, but it is not inferior either.
Journal of Bone and Joint Surgery
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 9-year follow-up is an important part of a randomized trial in patients with CLBP.
a substantial proportion of the patients allocated either to lumbar fusion or to cognitive intervention and exercise had crossed over.
lumbar fusion does not seem to be the best way to treat patients with chronic low-back pain.
